# Route Contract

This reference defines the owner-visible navigation surface shared by every public
Ultra Skill. A Route Card is a derived observation from canonical project files, Git,
and the current run. It is not workflow authority, a stage marker, or permission to
continue.

## Route Card

Show a `UBP Route Card` at entry, at a material checkpoint, when pausing or
blocked, at the observable exit, and before moving to another public Skill. The default
rendering of that card is the compact progress expression below; the full field set is
reserved for the moments listed there. Keep an unchanged field short, but never omit an
unresolved decision or unfinished obligation.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Route` | The current public Skill, or `idle` when no workflow is active |
| `Mode` | One mode declared by that Skill |
| `Why` | The current problem or evidence gap |
| `Outcome` | The owner-visible result this route is trying to produce |
| `Accepted boundary` | Accepted scope, exclusions, and authority that cover this run |
| `Position` | Artifact-derived navigation such as selected reports or remaining tasks |
| `Exit condition` | Observable evidence or owner decision that ends this mode |
| `Delta` | Material facts changed since the prior card |
| `Reality` | Live path, verification state, fakes, limitations, and unknowns |
| `Decision needed` | One material owner decision, or `none` |
| `Next` | The smallest covered continuation or one recommended public route |
| `Not done` | Obligations left at a pause or exit |

`Position` may report exact mechanical observations such as selected lenses with
reports, dependency-ready tasks, or an ACP session waiting for permission. Never turn a
count, validator result, finding total, or transport event into semantic progress or a
numeric completion score.

### Compact progress expression

The default owner-visible rendering of the card is five lines built from current
evidence:

| Line | Derived from | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Goal` | `Why` + `Outcome` | The outcome this route is trying to produce, in one sentence |
| `Verified result` | `Position` + `Reality` | Only what current evidence verifies; a completion claim names the evidence that verifies it |
| `Gap` | `Exit condition` + `Not done` | What still separates this run from its exit |
| `Next action` | `Next` | The smallest covered continuation; a planned item is a future action, never a result |
| `Owner decision needed` | `Decision needed` | One material decision, or `none`; do not invent one to fill the line |

The compact expression is a rendering of the Route Card, not a second schema, state
center, or mandatory UI format: every line is derived from the card, which is itself
derived from canonical files, Git, and the current run. A transport return, task count,
structural validation, or reused old evidence is never a `Verified result`; an unknown
stays visibly unknown and is never displayed as success.

The compact form is the default at entry, during ordinary progress, at an ordinary exit
of the current mode, and across transitions covered by the accepted boundary — including
an ordinary Status answer, which is itself the entry and exit of a read-only route.
Show the full card — not the compact form — at a material checkpoint, when pausing or
blocked, and whenever the owner asks for route, grant, or authority detail; that detail
stays one explicit question away instead of being volunteered every turn.

Compaction never hides substance: an unresolved decision, a material boundary change, or
missing authorization stays visible in `Owner decision needed`, `Gap`, and
`Verified result`, and the related fields expand whenever the five lines cannot carry
them truthfully. A real failure or unknown is reported as fact, never as success, and an
ordinary failed check inside an already authorized repair boundary updates
`Verified result` and `Gap` without manufacturing a new owner decision.

## Material checkpoints

Stop and obtain the Owner's current decision before any of these changes or effects:

1. a new or reduced North Star, specification, or Change commitment;
2. a material delta to an active Change outcome, acceptance, non-goal, or public seam;
3. evidence that materially changes the feasible direction or product boundary;
4. wider Execution Grant scope, effects, budget, expiry, or Agent/provider topology;
5. transfer of the canonical writer;
6. unresolved P0/P1, risk acceptance, or the same root cause surviving three failed fixes;
7. finalization, archive, commit, push, tag, publication, deployment, real installation,
   credentials, provider spend, or another external or irreversible effect.

A current explicit owner request that itself names the change or effect is the Owner's
current decision for that delta: proceed under it and do not re-ask confirmation of
what was just requested. The checkpoint still applies to any delta the request does not
name — silently reducing an existing promise, widening effects, or re-scoping untouched
work still returns to the owner.

Naming, internal design, ordinary technical choices, task decomposition, covered local
edits and tests, and non-material evidence reconciliation remain model-owned inside the
accepted boundary. Do not ask for confirmation when `Decision needed` is `none`.

Deciding how something works stays model-owned; deciding that it destroys what someone
already has does not. When such a choice would overwrite, truncate, delete, or replace
existing bytes or state — this run's own write, or the behavior the delivered code will
perform for its users — take the non-destructive form of the same choice and keep going:
create exclusively, write a separate target, or refuse the collision and report it. That
default needs no question, and an effect the owner already authorized for exactly this
data stays authorized. Only when no non-destructive form can deliver the named outcome
is the destruction a material trade-off, surfaced as one question with a recommendation.

## Continuation

Public modes belong to one of three invocation classes; model-only disciplines form a
fourth class:

| Invocation class | Owner entry | Model continuation |
|---|---:|---:|
| `explicit-entry` | yes | no |
| `grant-continuable` | yes | only under a valid Execution Grant covering that mode |
| `router` | yes | no; the Owner invokes read-only diagnosis explicitly |
| `model-discipline` | no | only as an internal method of a covered workflow |

Host metadata is only a coarse discovery bit. Before continuing, the Skill itself must
verify its selected mode, the same active `change_id`, the valid Execution Grant,
allowed local effects, stop conditions, and any material checkpoint. A coarse Host bit
never permits an explicit-entry mode. Without a covering grant, stop with a Route Card
and recommend the exact explicit route; never invoke another public Skill merely because
its files appear ready.

Discovery is not authority, and withheld discovery is not a guard. Two Hosts expose no
routing bit at all, so a public route is discoverable to the model wherever the Owner
could reach it in one request — including a route whose modes are all `explicit-entry`.
Loading such a Skill only lets it check its own entry: it proceeds when the Owner's
current request names that work, and otherwise reports what it observed and stops. The
bit stays off only where the product requires the Owner to name the route explicitly —
read-only Status diagnosis and Delegate's owner-authorized worker topology — and on a
Host without the bit those two routes rest on the same in-Skill check.

A current explicit owner request is Owner entry for the work it names even when an
active Change, an expired grant, or an unfinished closeout exists: those are older
obligations of the older work, reported in `Not done` and gated only at their own
steps — never preconditions for executing the current request.

### Open closeout obligations

That branch is executable, not a promise. An absent or unaccepted North Star, a trace
with no accepted revision to resolve against, an expired grant, and an unfinished formal
review are open closeout obligations. Each gates exactly the step that produces it — an
acceptance or completion claim, task closeout, finalization, archive, or an external
effect — and otherwise stays visible in `Not done` and `Gap` while the decomposition,
implementation, and verification the current request covers proceed. Implementing a
decision the owner already stated explicitly is that covered work; a strategic choice
this run composed is an open decision and is surfaced as one, never as settled input.
Carrying an obligation openly is the honest branch: fabricating an acceptance, marking a
draft accepted, or recording a provisional workflow state to get past it is not.

Two things are not open obligations. Work that would breach a constraint the owner has
actually accepted, or reduce a promise the specifications already made, is the material
checkpoint above: reconcile it with the owner before the conflicting step. And durable
authorization is never inferred from files — a recorded grant, an old task, an archived
Change, or a stored quote is inactive data until the owner's current message or the
grant contract's own verification makes it live.

Within an accepted Change and valid grant, show the Route Card before each public Skill
transition and continue without a confirmation question only when the next mode and all
effects are covered. A material checkpoint still pauses. `Next` is either `continue:
<route>/<mode>` when covered or `recommend: <route>/<mode>` when owner invocation is
required.

Execution events such as tool calls, plans, usage, permission requests, worker output,
ACP updates, and process termination are transport observations. They may populate
`Position`, `Delta`, or `Reality`; they never decide acceptance, task completion, or the
next semantic route.

## Recovery and degraded diagnosis

On a fresh session or Host, reconstruct the card from the accepted North Star, Project
Brief, active Change authority, task ledger and matching contexts, decisions, evidence,
Git, and current installation/runtime observations. Read the closing `## Resume Note`
for only the current work package. Do not rerun completed Research or create a route
ledger to remember where the conversation stopped.

If authority is absent, ambiguous, stale, malformed, or temporarily unreadable, stop
semantic writes but keep read-only diagnosis reachable. Report the exact fact that
prevents a normal route and the cheapest safe repair, retry, cancel, abandon, or fresh
session path. Never describe a blocked route as an endless in-progress workflow.

Owner revisions remain recoverable: edit a draft in place, supersede an accepted
decision with a new owner record, and preserve Git/history. Status may summarize that
history on request, but no event log becomes a second source of truth.

When context pressure threatens reliable continuation, finish the nearest safe write,
refresh the canonical context's Resume Note, show a final card, and recommend a fresh
session. Context size is an observation, not a hard semantic gate.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mnotes — a single-person archive for meeting notes, built for one job:
find a past decision by keyword and see which day it was recorded.

Stdlib only. Nothing leaves this machine. Source files are only ever read.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

TEXT_SUFFIXES = {".md", ".markdown", ".txt", ".text"}

# Search is a substring scan in SQL, not a full-text index. Ceiling: fine for one
# person's notes (tens of thousands of entries scan in well under a second); it
# degrades linearly past that. Upgrade path: an FTS5 index — but NOT the trigram
# tokenizer, which silently returns zero hits for two-character Chinese keywords
# like 预算 or 决定. A CJK-aware tokenizer (jieba/ICU) would be required, which
# means a dependency this version deliberately avoids.
SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (
    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    occurred_on  TEXT NOT NULL,
    title        TEXT NOT NULL,
    body         TEXT NOT NULL,
    source       TEXT NOT NULL,
    content_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (source, content_hash)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS notes_by_day ON notes (occurred_on DESC);
"""


def today():
    return datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def default_db():
    return os.environ.get("MNOTES_DB") or str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "notes.db")


def connect(path):
    Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn


def parse_day(text):
    """Return a normalized YYYY-MM-DD, or None if it is not a real date."""
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d").strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    except ValueError:
        return None


def day_from_filename(name):
    for pattern, fmt in ((r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", "%Y-%m-%d"), (r"\d{8}", "%Y%m%d")):
        match = re.search(pattern, name)
        if not match:
            continue
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(match.group(), fmt).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return None


def title_from_filename(stem):
    """The heading already prints the day, so drop a leading date from the title."""
    trimmed = re.sub(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{8})[\s_.-]*", "", stem)
    return trimmed or stem


def first_line(body):
    for line in body.splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            return line.strip().lstrip("# ").strip() or "(无标题)"
    return "(无标题)"


def store(conn, *, occurred_on, title, body, source):
    """Insert a note. Returns its id, or None when this exact content from this
    exact source is already archived. Never updates or deletes an existing row."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    cursor = conn.execute(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notes"
        " (occurred_on, title, body, source, content_hash, created_at)"
        " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (occurred_on, title, body, source, digest, datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")),
    )
    conn.commit()
    return cursor.lastrowid if cursor.rowcount else None


def search(conn, keywords):
    clauses = " AND ".join(["(title || char(10) || body) LIKE '%' || ? || '%'"] * len(keywords))
    return conn.execute(
        f"SELECT * FROM notes WHERE {clauses} ORDER BY occurred_on DESC, id DESC",
        list(keywords),
    ).fetchall()


def matching_lines(body, keywords, limit=3):
    lowered = [k.lower() for k in keywords]
    hits = [line.strip() for line in body.splitlines()
            if line.strip() and any(k in line.lower() for k in lowered)]
    if not hits:
        hits = [first_line(body)]
    return hits[:limit], len(hits) > limit


def note_heading(row):
    return f"#{row['id']}  {row['occurred_on']}  {row['title']}"


# --- commands ---------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_add(args, stdin):
    body = (args.message if args.message is not None else stdin.read()).strip("\n")
    if not body.strip():
        print("笔记是空的，没有存。用 --message 传内容，或把内容从标准输入喂进来。")
        return 2

    occurred_on = today() if args.date is None else parse_day(args.date)
    if occurred_on is None:
        print(f"日期 {args.date!r} 认不出来，请用 YYYY-MM-DD，例如 2026-09-08。")
        return 2

    title = args.title.strip() if args.title else first_line(body)
    conn = connect(args.db)
    note_id = store(conn, occurred_on=occurred_on, title=title, body=body, source="stdin")
    if note_id is None:
        print(f"这条内容已经存过了（{occurred_on}  {title}），没有重复存。")
        return 0
    print(f"已存 #{note_id}  {occurred_on}  {title}")
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, stdin):
    root = Path(args.path).expanduser()
    if not root.exists():
        print(f"找不到 {root}，没有导入任何东西。")
        return 2

    if root.is_file():
        candidates = [root]
    else:
        candidates = sorted(p for p in root.rglob("*")
                            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in TEXT_SUFFIXES)

    conn = connect(args.db)
    imported = skipped = unreadable = 0
    for path in candidates:
        try:
            body = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip("\n")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            unreadable += 1
            print(f"  读不了，跳过：{path}")
            continue
        if not body.strip():
            skipped += 1
            continue
        occurred_on = day_from_filename(path.name) or datetime.fromtimestamp(
            path.stat().st_mtime).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        title = title_from_filename(path.stem)
        note_id = store(conn, occurred_on=occurred_on, title=title,
                        body=body, source=str(path.resolve()))
        if note_id is None:
            skipped += 1
        else:
            imported += 1
            print(f"  + #{note_id}  {occurred_on}  {title}")

    print(f"导入 {imported} 条，跳过 {skipped} 条（已存在或为空），读不了 {unreadable} 个文件。")
    print("原文件一个字都没改。")
    return 0


def cmd_find(args, stdin):
    conn = connect(args.db)
    rows = search(conn, args.keywords)
    if not rows:
        print(f"没有找到同时含 {' '.join(args.keywords)} 的记录。")
        return 1

    for row in rows:
        print(note_heading(row))
        lines, truncated = matching_lines(row["body"], args.keywords)
        for line in lines:
            print(f"    {line}")
        if truncated:
            print(f"    …（还有更多命中，用 show {row['id']} 看全文）")
        if row["source"] != "stdin":
            print(f"    来源：{row['source']}")
        print()
    print(f"共 {len(rows)} 条。")
    return 0


def cmd_show(args, stdin):
    conn = connect(args.db)
    row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = ?", (args.id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        print(f"没有 #{args.id} 这条记录。")
        return 1
    print(note_heading(row))
    if row["source"] != "stdin":
        print(f"来源：{row['source']}")
    print("-" * 40)
    print(row["body"])
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, stdin):
    conn = connect(args.db)
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM notes ORDER BY occurred_on DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?", (args.limit,)
    ).fetchall()
    if not rows:
        print("还没有任何记录。用 add 存一条，或用 import 把已有的文件导进来。")
        return 0
    for row in rows:
        print(note_heading(row))
    return 0


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="mnotes", description="会议记录归档与关键词检索（单机、单人）")
    parser.add_argument("--db", default=default_db(), help="数据库路径（默认 ./data/notes.db）")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    add = sub.add_parser("add", help="存一条会议记录（内容来自 --message 或标准输入）")
    add.add_argument("-m", "--message", help="记录正文；省略则从标准输入读取")
    add.add_argument("-d", "--date", help="这条是哪天记的，YYYY-MM-DD，默认今天")
    add.add_argument("-t", "--title", help="标题，默认取正文第一行")
    add.set_defaults(func=cmd_add)

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="把已有的 .md/.txt 文件导进来（只读原文件）")
    imp.add_argument("path", help="一个文件或一个目录（目录会递归）")
    imp.set_defaults(func=cmd_import)

    find = sub.add_parser("find", help="按关键词找回记录，结果带日期")
    find.add_argument("keywords", nargs="+", help="多个关键词是「都要命中」")
    find.set_defaults(func=cmd_find)

    show = sub.add_parser("show", help="按编号看某条记录的全文")
    show.add_argument("id", type=int)
    show.set_defaults(func=cmd_show)

    listing = sub.add_parser("list", help="按日期倒序列出最近的记录")
    listing.add_argument("-n", "--limit", type=int, default=20)
    listing.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)

    return parser


def main(argv=None, stdin=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:])
    return args.func(args, stdin if stdin is not None else sys.stdin)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests for mnotes: the owner's acceptance is "find a past decision by keyword and
see which day it was recorded", so every test here asserts against that."""

import contextlib
import io
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import mnotes


def run(*argv, stdin=""):
    """Run the CLI, returning (exit_code, stdout)."""
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
        code = mnotes.main(list(argv), stdin=io.StringIO(stdin))
    return code, out.getvalue()


class NotesTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.tmp = Path(self._tmp.name)
        self.db = self.tmp / "notes.db"
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)

    def add(self, body, **kw):
        argv = ["--db", str(self.db), "add"]
        for key, value in kw.items():
            argv += ["--" + key.replace("_", "-"), value]
        return run(*argv, stdin=body)


class TestAddAndFind(NotesTestCase):
    def test_find_two_character_chinese_keyword(self):
        self.add("我们决定把预算砍掉一半，下周上线", date="2026-09-08", title="周会")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "预算")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("预算砍掉一半", out)

    def test_find_reports_the_day_it_was_recorded(self):
        self.add("决定延后发布", date="2026-09-08", title="周会")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "延后")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("2026-09-08", out)

    def test_multiple_keywords_must_all_match(self):
        self.add("决定砍预算", date="2026-09-01", title="A")
        self.add("决定加人力", date="2026-09-02", title="B")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "决定", "预算")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("砍预算", out)
        self.assertNotIn("加人力", out)

    def test_ascii_keyword_is_case_insensitive(self):
        self.add("Decided to ship on Friday", date="2026-09-03", title="Standup")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "DECIDED")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("Friday", out)

    def test_no_match_says_so_and_exits_nonzero(self):
        self.add("决定砍预算", date="2026-09-01", title="A")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "招聘")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIn("没有", out)

    def test_defaults_to_today_when_no_date_given(self):
        self.add("随手记一条")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "随手")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn(mnotes.today(), out)

    def test_title_falls_back_to_first_line(self):
        self.add("季度复盘\n结论：不改架构")
        code, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "不改架构")
        self.assertIn("季度复盘", out)

    def test_rejects_malformed_date(self):
        code, out = self.add("x", date="2026/09/08")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2)
        self.assertIn("YYYY-MM-DD", out)

    def test_rejects_empty_note(self):
        code, out = self.add("   \n  \n")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2)
        self.assertIn("空", out)

    def test_show_prints_the_full_body(self):
        self.add("第一行\n第二行\n第三行", date="2026-09-08", title="长会")
        _, out = run("--db", str(self.db), "find", "第二行")

# mnotes — 会议记录归档 + 关键词检索

只干一件事：**过后按关键词把「上次那个决定」找出来，并且看得到是哪天记的。**

单人、单机、纯 Python 标准库，没有任何依赖，不联网，不共享。

## 用起来

```bash
chmod +x mnotes.py        # 只需一次
```

### 1. 把已有的散记导进来（原文件只读，一个字都不改）

路径由你给，工具不内置任何默认扫描目录：

```bash
./mnotes.py import ~/Documents/会议
./mnotes.py import ~/Desktop/周会.md      # 单个文件也行
```

- 递归找 `.md` `.markdown` `.txt` `.text`
- 日期优先取文件名里的 `2026-09-08` 或 `20260908`，取不到就用文件修改时间
- 重复导入不会重复入库；原文件改过之后再导，会**新增一条**，旧措辞仍然搜得到

### 2. 开会时随手记

```bash
./mnotes.py add -m "决定：Q4 预算砍一半，先保上线"
./mnotes.py add -d 2026-09-08 -t "产品周会"      # 补录，正文从标准输入读
```

省略 `-d` 就是今天；省略 `-t` 就取正文第一行当标题。

### 3. 找回来（核心）

```bash
./mnotes.py find 预算
./mnotes.py find 决定 供应商     # 多个关键词 = 都要命中
```

输出长这样，日期就在编号旁边：

```
#4  2026-09-08  临时对齐
    决定：预算的事下周一给最终版

#1  2026-08-12  产品周会
    决定：把 Q4 预算砍掉一半，先保上线
    来源：/Users/you/Documents/会议/2026-08-12-产品周会.md
```

只打印命中的那几行。要全文：

```bash
./mnotes.py show 1
./mnotes.py list -n 30           # 按日期倒序看最近的
```

找不到时会明说，并返回退出码 1（方便你写脚本）。

## 笔记库放在哪

默认 `./data/notes.db`（一个 SQLite 文件）。想换地方：

```bash
export MNOTES_DB=~/Dropbox/notes.db
# 或每次： ./mnotes.py --db /path/to/notes.db find 预算
```

备份就是复制这一个文件。

## 两个说明白的取舍

**检索用子串扫描，不是全文索引。** 因为实测 SQLite FTS5 的 trigram 分词对「预算」
「决定」这类两字中文词**返回 0 条命中**——正是你最可能搜的词。子串匹配中英文都准，
单人几万条笔记的规模下毫秒级。真到明显变慢时，升级路径是接 CJK 分词器（jieba/ICU）
的 FTS5 索引，代价是引入依赖。

**只做归档和检索，不自动提炼待办/责任人/截止日。** 你给的成功判据只要求找回决定本身，
这项没被要求，也没被排除——需要的话再加。

```bash
python3 -m unittest test_mnotes -v      # 25 项
```

| `resume` | One exact task id carried by this invocation, or a valid Execution Grant covering the unique in-progress task | Existing work is reconciled from Git, context, and Resume Note, then reaches the same completion evidence or a typed stop | Recommend the next exact task, `ultra-test/audit`, or the responsible repair route |
| `reopen` | One exact task id carried by this invocation, or a valid Execution Grant after current evidence invalidates a completed task | The invalidated criteria are refreshed through a new review and the task is completed again, or the remaining gate is named | Recommend the next exact task or `ultra-test/reaudit` |

first implementation edit, at material checkpoints or unavailable evidence, and after

## Before you start

Fill in the task context's Implementation section as prose a person can read:
which modules change, how the interfaces move, which seam the tests will use.
Confirm that, then write code. Deciding the design while typing implementation

## Develop through red then green

Follow `../ultra-tdd/SKILL.md`, writing tests only on the seams the plan already
confirmed, one slice at a time. `ultra-review` owns evidence-backed refactoring when
observed duplication, coupling, or a boundary defect justifies it; a slice count does
not make that decision.

## Converge on the task-scoped acceptance set

Development ends when every task-scoped criterion has its required current evidence and
responsible semantic disposition, not merely when commands pass or the code looks
finished. Resolve the context's **Change Acceptance IDs** against the active `intent.md`
for `<change_id>`. For each named row consume its exact `Verification type` and
`Required evidence`. When one outcome needs more than one authority, split it into
independent criteria with unique IDs and preserve each authority separately; every row
has exactly one verification type. Task-local acceptance may add evidence requirements,
but it does not replace or narrow the Change mapping.

Handle the four verification types without converting one authority into another:

- Execute only `command` observations. Record the exact command, working directory,
  exit status, retained raw output reference, and its exact SHA-256.
- For `inspection`, cite the exact source and revision or digest, then refresh the
  observation after any touched source changes.
- For `owner-judgment`, preserve the cited owner decision. The owner alone supplies its
  semantic result; a model statement, validator, score, or command cannot proxy it.
- For `external-observation`, preserve the provider or system receipt without proxying it
  with a local command, model claim, or synthetic fixture, and bind its exact bytes by
  SHA-256.

- Missing `owner-judgment` stops at its named owner gate.
- Missing `external-observation` stops at its named external or authorization gate.
- If an inspection exists but its semantic implication is unresolved, stop at the
  responsible model or owner gate; a structural citation is not an automatic acceptance
  verdict.

Run one baseline before repairing anything. Track a best-ever evidence set keyed by
criterion, verification type, and source identity to make progress visible, plus the
current evidence set used for convergence. Stale or regressed evidence remains history
but cannot satisfy the current set. Do not infer semantic progress or failure from a
round count. The loop has three explicit exits:

| Exit | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Converged | Every mapped and task-local criterion has current required evidence of every named type, and the responsible model or owner has made any semantic disposition | Close out below |
| Stalled | An in-scope repair yields no new or refreshed evidence and no further evidence-producing repair is justified inside the approved task | Stop; report the missing evidence, the attempted repair, and the responsible next gate |
| Unreachable | Required evidence cannot be observed because an executable, fixture, provider, service, declared environment prerequisite, or required authorization is unavailable | Stop that criterion; report the unavailable prerequisite or gate and its reachable repair path |

A nonzero command exit is an observation, not automatically `Unreachable`; inspect its
output and repair within scope when justified. None of these exits mechanically decides
semantic sufficiency, owner acceptance, or external truth.

## Answer the six evidence dimensions

Each has a rule you can check against the work rather than assert:

| Dimension | Answered when |
|---|---|
| `tests_written` | This diff adds or changes at least one assertion — touching a test file is not enough |
| `tests_passed` | The last test run exited zero and covered the files this diff touched |
| `persistence_real` | On any path that stores data, the test uses real storage or a container |
| `feature_flags_audit` | No flag on this change's execution path defaults to off, including flags this task did not add but now depends on |
| `vertical_slice` | One test's execution path runs from the entry point through to persistence |
| `spec_trace` | The anchor the task's `trace_to` names exists in the specification |

Before task review, retain the actual criterion evidence, raw logs, owner records,
external receipts, and cited artifacts without inventing another completion record.
Do not write `evidence.json` before the task's validated final `SUMMARY.json` exists.
The review packet admits those actual pre-review observations together with the ledger,
context acceptance, and packet-defined task scope. A structural validator may check
exact fields, types, digests, paths, and freshness observations. It never supplies an
acceptance disposition, turns a model claim into command evidence, or decides semantic pass.
Evidence is a sensor: a gap or legacy v1 record is reported with a migration
diagnostic, never rewritten as v2 truth.

## When implementation and the specification disagree

This is the one backward edge in the whole workflow. Classify before touching the
specification, and classify by outcome rather than reason: does every commitment
the specification already made still hold afterwards? If even one no longer holds
it is a REDUCTION — stop and ask the owner, however good the argument. Log the
classification in the context file's Change Log.

## Close out

Keep the ledger row `in_progress` while running task review through
`../ultra-review/SKILL.md`. Build its immutable packet from the ledger, task context,

# Write one failing test on a seam, then just enough code to pass it

Without feedback from code that actually ran, the work is blind flying. This is
the loop that supplies it, and it serves Goal 3, Production-Ready.

## Before you start

1. When called from a planned Change, read
   `../ultra-change/references/change-contract.md` and apply its **Active Change
   authority resolution** before reading any active `intent.md`, resolving the current
   `change_id` or task, reading its context, running the baseline, or executing red-green
   product edits. A stable zero result stops with no current task; any typed diagnostic,
   including non-unique authority, stops with its repair before the baseline, red-green,
   or any product write. After one valid authority, read its intent, `.ultra/tasks.json`,
   and the matching current task context for the seams confirmed during planning. For a
   micro edit outside the Ultra lifecycle, no active task context is required; use the
   accepted request, maintained specification, and an existing repository seam, and
   create no Ultra task or delivery claim.
2. Run the repository's existing test command once, unchanged, to see what
   passing currently looks like. Read `references/test-execution.md` before recording
   that run or any red/green evidence.
3. Read `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary — test names carry the domain words.

## Definition of done

- One slice is complete: one seam, one test, one minimal implementation.
- The test was observed failing before the implementation existed, and observed
  passing after. Both runs are real command output.
- The test reads as a specification of behavior through a public interface, and
  survives replacing the implementation underneath it.

## Seams, and what a good test on one looks like

A seam is a place where behavior can change without editing at that place — the
module interface. Tests live on seams and never reach for internals. Prefer a
seam that already exists, take the highest one that works, and one is the ideal
number. Verify behavior through that public interface: a name like "user can
checkout with a valid cart" shows at a glance what capability exists, and one
logical assertion per test keeps it readable.

## Red, then green

Write the failing test first and run it, so that red is observed rather than
assumed. Then write the smallest code that turns it green. Predict no later
tests and add no speculative capability. Then take the next slice.

Refactoring is not part of this loop; `ultra-review` owns it when observed duplication,
coupling, or a boundary defect supplies evidence that restructuring is worthwhile.

## Three patterns that produce tests worth deleting

| Pattern | How you recognize it |
|---|---|
| Implementation-coupled | Mocks an internal collaborator, tests a private method, asserts on call counts or ordering, or reaches past the interface into the database. The check: behavior is unchanged after restructuring, yet the test breaks. |
| Tautological | Recomputes the expected value the same way the implementation does, so it can never fail. Expected values come from an independent source — a known literal, a hand-worked example, the specification. |
| All tests first | Writing every test before any implementation tests imagined behavior. It captures shape rather than user-visible behavior, is insensitive to real change, and freezes the test structure before the implementation is understood. Take one test, one implementation, and repeat. |

## Mock only at the system boundary

External APIs, time and randomness, sometimes the filesystem. Prefer a real test
library over mocking the database. Your own classes, modules and internal
collaborators stay real.

Design for that boundary: inject dependencies, and give each external operation
its own named function rather than one generic fetcher — mocking then needs no
conditional logic, and which endpoints a test touches stays visible. When a real
dependency is the right answer, copy
`references/templates/testcontainer-postgres.ts` or
`references/templates/testcontainer-postgres.py`, and
`references/templates/vertical-slice.ts` for a path that runs end to end.

## When the owner decides

Weakening an assertion, skipping a relevant test, or adjusting an expected value
to obtain green output crosses the C5 boundary — stop and surface it. A test that
is genuinely wrong about the specification is a specification question, so it
goes to the owner as one.

- `../ultra-change/references/change-contract.md` — canonical Active Change authority resolution.

- `references/templates/README.md` — read when choosing which enabling template
  fits the dependency you need to make real.
